newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Swiss seen vulnerable to big losses.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Swiss seen vulnerable to big losses.

text.p: The dollar made a significant technical rally against the Swiss franc, punching out a two-year high, and the Swiss looks vulnerable to even broader losses, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
Mark/Swiss has also climbed to just below a 100-month moving average at 0.8585, and chartists said a break there could yield a quick pop to the upside.
"We are looking at a setup for what could be a spectacular run in mark/Swiss and dollar/Swiss," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc.

Dollar/Swiss was struggling to close above a trendline from 1989 which comes through at 1.3295. In addition, chartists spied triangle patterns in dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss that suggest the recent rallies will continue.
"That usually means we'll get one more thrust to the upside. We should see another push toward 1.5735 marks," said Joseph Klettner, foreign exchange technician at Chase Securities Inc.
Interim support comes in just below 1.55 marks, with the near-term upside objective pegged at 1.5820. Dollar/Swiss could have legs to test 1.3415 and 1.3520, chartists said.
Dollar/yen looks less bullish, thanks partly to the weak profile of mark/yen and Swiss/yen, chartists said.
"This is a dollar-friendly environment, but not so much in dollar/yen, which has mark/yen weighing on it," Morden said.

The greenback enjoys good support at 113.30/40, which could allow a revisit to the double-top resistance near 114.90. But the dollar will face heavy selling before then, with near-term resistance coming in at 114.30/40 yen, chartists said.
"I don't think we're ready to go through 115 (yen) yet. I'd sell above 114.50," Morden said.
Mark/yen survived its latest test of support at 73.05, but looks vulnerable to a slump toward 72.65 before any rally toward 74, chartists said.
"Mark/yen is due for a pullback, though the picture is not very clear," Klettner said.
In other trade, chartists noted sterling should continue its recent rally toward $1.58 and 2.60 marks.
